utterances.text: Does it follow from this sentence further that the information received from either Kiseljak or Tuzla, it is irrelevant at this point, also contained the piece of information that the mayor and the Bobovac Brigade commander were relieved of their duties?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no. I don't know which commander they said would have take the command off. If it was the commander before the 23rd or after the 23rd. That's -- that was something we was wondering about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. But what I need to clarify with you now is whether this information concerning the relieving of duty was in fact conveyed in the telefax received from either Kiseljak or Tuzla. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't remember if it came directly from Kiseljak or from Tuzla, but I have it in a fax.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please look at document P 06063, which is also contained in the Prosecutor's set of documents. Have you found it, Mr. Birger?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that this is the order issued by General Petkovic that you referred to in your diary in the entry for the 25th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please look at another document in the Prosecutor's set of material, P 06049.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have you found it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This is a letter from the HVO liaison officer, Vinko Lucic, sent to the Kiseljak command. We have already analysed this when you were

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From the introductory part of this letter, does it not follow that UNPROFOR sought assistance concerning the investigation about the alleged massacre over the Muslim population in Vares municipality? This is in fact what the first sentence reads, does it not?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which line are you talking to in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: The very beginning of the text. [In English] "Regarding your request for assistance in connection with the investigation," et cetera. [Interpretation] Is that right? Does it not follow from this text that UNPROFOR sought assistance in the investigation into the events at Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading --

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, just look at the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I suppose you will agree that the letter was dated 24th of October, 1993. I suppose that's not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is write -- written up in the page.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Can we agree that at the time on the 24th of October, 1993, for someone who was at Kiseljak as Vinko Lucic was, that person could not really have been aware of what had actually transpired at Stupni Do? Can we agree about that?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I had no contact with this liaison officer, so it was not a contact I talked to. So I don't know why -- where he was and how he work.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I'm asking you this, Mr. Birger, because in connection with the second but last paragraph of this letter you said, when answering Mr. Mundis's question, that you were not really clear about why this had been written this way. I'm asking you now whether Vinko Lucic, on the 24th of October, practically wanted to say that still there were no verified information about any offensive activities by the HVO in the area of Vares and the alleged massacre in the village of Stupni Do. Would this make it clearer for you why this sentence was written?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I've never seen this paper before in Bosnia. I seen it now when I came here, and I have no -- it was not in my level. It was over the battalion commander level, this discussion is. It's in BH command, BH command, command -- my battalion commander. So it's over my level.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, you saw this document for the first time here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I suppose then in that case you wouldn't know which order by General Petkovic concerning the situation in Vares is being referred to in this letter, which order was attached to the letter written by Lucic from the Kiseljak command.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must -- I don't understand what you meaning. I have a letter from Petkovic to the Bobovac Brigade. Yes, I have read this paper. This paper, I haven't seen. Again, it's highest, over my level.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. If you didn't see the letter, then one can infer that you wouldn't know which order was referred to here even if it was the order we saw on -- at that document, P 06063. It would follow quite logically that you wouldn't know which order was attached to this letter. Can you just confirm to me that you, in fact, don't know?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I could only read the order, and I couldn't know what he have for information to give this order, that's correct, yes. I don't know what he would have for information. It's impossibility for me to know.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, I should in fact like to know if you were aware of the fact that in addition to Lucic's letter or annexed to it was the order that we saw a moment ago marked with the number P 06063. I should like to know if you know about this or if you in fact have no knowledge of this at all.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the order, I have seen before. I have this order in paper to my camp orders, but it's two different papers. This paper I've never seen. I've seen the order from Petkovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I will try once again because we are obviously not understanding each other. I understand what you're saying, but I would like to know the following: Do you have any information that the order you just saw, which was under number P 06063, whether you knew that this order was delivered as part of Lucic's letter? Do you know about this or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this letter.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: All right. All right. I'd like to ask you now to look at my set of documents and look for P 06144.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Can you explain what kind of document that is? What is it?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it's sent from BH command in Kiseljak, and, as I said before, that command is the command who my battalion belonged to. And also the drafter is Brigadier Ramsay. Ramsay was the Chief of Staff for BH command.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Can we agree, Mr. Birger, that this message is in fact a notification of a meeting that UNPROFOR representatives in Kiseljak held with General Petkovic on the 25th of October, 1993? That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only now read this paper on the top of the page is from command of Kiseljak, and again it's higher level over my command. I was not involved in negotiation in this level.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, I'm not going to ask you anything about that, but I believe that this document contains some information that is consistent with what you have told us so far. I just wanted to compare the documents we have at our disposal and find the consistencies. It says that a meeting was held at 2200 hours, paragraph 1. Mr. Petkovic came with his associates Lucic and Bandic, and that he had been staying in Kiseljak for some days as he had been unable to fly back to Split because of bad weather. We agree that this is written here. Of course you don't know anything about it, but this will be important for our later analysis. Now, please let's look together at paragraph 2, "Vares/Stupni Do." To avoid reading aloud, maybe we could read it for ourselves and then discuss it. If you have read it --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it now.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Tell me when you finish.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not finish. I'm finish.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: It is recorded here that General Petkovic had issued a written permit for UNPROFOR to go to Stupni Do, and that General Petkovic said that it made no sense to try to cover up anything, because, if something happened, that will be identified and determined. Do we agree that is written there?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see what's written here.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: There's written permit mentioned here. Was it a document that you saw yourself and you showed to the commander of the Vares Brigade, Kresimir Bozic? We saw it today under P 0 --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that document what you ...

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: All right. We will deal with this document in greater detail later, but now we will move on to another document in the Prosecutor's set, number P 06117. Could you please look at point 7. I'm not going to go through the whole document, because the Prosecutor has dealt with it earlier. Point 7 says: "HVO commander General Petkovic sent two documents to his subordinated units, one in which he proclaims a cease-fire in Vares area, and another one in which he orders Ante Pejcinovic, Duznovic, and Gavran be removed from their current positions." Have you found these documents?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Tell us, do you have any knowledge about the documents contained here?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not knowledge, but I know a little bit about the situation. I think it was the 24th or 23rd of -- 24th, I think, of October. I was going up to the Bobovac Brigade, and the police command, I think the name was Gavran or something like this.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, just a second. I would now like to focus on the documents alone, and very soon we'll move on to the situation on the ground and you'll tell us what you know. Can I therefore conclude that you have no knowledge about these two documents? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only seen the document, the orders from Petkovic. I never seen other documents.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Could you clarify, since we have information that one of these documents was produced, in fact, by you, could you look at P 06022. Could you tell me, Mr. Birger, have you seen this document ever before?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't remember I had seen that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: In your diary for 26 October 1993, which is the day to which this document P 06177 we discussed earlier relates, it's clear you didn't receive any documents from Petkovic, from Travnik, Kiseljak, or any other town. If you want to check in your diary you can, but I have already checked, and there's nothing recorded for that day. Your diary's number P 02980. Is that so? Did you have time to --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: All right. We don't have that much time --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it. 26. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: There's quite a lot of writing for the 26th. My question was that you did not record on the 26th that you received the mentioned two documents from General Petkovic from any of the other UNPROFOR commands. When I say "mention," I mean the two documents from the Prosecutor's Exhibit P 0617 -- sorry, P 06117. If it's too complicated to check that now we can move on, because we don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I want to say before I haven't written every -- written this diary. I have leave -- I have a statement of these days, and the statement is -- is what I have signed. I -- this is summary of the days. We have not written everything in this diary.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Birger, could we move to the actual situation, and I believe documents will help us in this exercise. If in addition to the direct answer to my question you wish to add anything, please tell me so and in view of the time constraints we'll find a way together to cover it in the best way. Look at P 06026. It's in my set of documents. P 06026. You found the document, I believe?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. So it's a notification by Ivica Rajic on combat activities in Vares from the 23rd October 1993. This document has already been viewed in this courtroom, and for the purposes of my examination, Mr. Birger, could we please focus at the beginning. In the upper right corner of the page we see the names of persons to whom this notification, this information, was addressed.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: In line two we see the name of my client. You see the name of Milivoj Petkovic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You see that above it says "Chief," which is wrong, but never mind, "Chief of the Main Staff of the HVO Mostar." Would it be correct to conclude that a copy of this report intended for General Petkovic was sent to Mostar? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Could we please try to remember that UNPROFOR document of the 26th of October, 1993, concerning a meeting held on the 25th of October, 1993, with General Petkovic, which says that General Petkovic was still in Kiseljak on that day because he was unable to fly to Split due to bad weather. On that basis, would it be correct to conclude that the person who sent this report believed that General Petkovic had left Kiseljak and that he was already in the base of the Main Staff of the HVO? It's a question of logics -- logic. Is that a correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He could know it, and he couldn't know it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look at the penultimate paragraph of this report by Ivica Rajic. It says: "Do to attempts --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm a bit confused. Maybe I have not understood, so I would like to be told. It says in the letter: "To the chief of the Main Staff, Mostar," and you are pointing out that the -- your client could not have left Kiseljak to go to Split. Now, the -- the person who put "Petkovic, Mostar" in the letter, it is irrelevant whether he knew whether your client had gone to Split or not. Because, anyway, there are three localities involved here? Am I wrong? Have I got it all wrong?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know that at this point everything still seems like an incoherent group of diversion elements, but I know that my client usually came to Kiseljak by an UNPROFOR aeroplane -- or, rather, helicopter, and, as a rule, it was a Split-Kiseljak flight. Then from Split he would go to Mostar, Citluk, or wherever he needed to go. That's why that document of the UNPROFOR mentions his return to Split rather than, let's say, Mostar. What I'm trying to show at this moment is this: That my client was supposed to leave Kiseljak earlier, that Ivica Rajic believed him to be gone from Kiseljak, and that because of that he was sending him a report to some other address. That will be later important for you to establish the existence of any communication between Ivica Rajic and General Petkovic. That's the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So, Witness -- Witness, if we can return to the conclusion of this report. "Due to attempts to obstruct the planned activities, I placed in isolation Ante Pejcinovic, Zvonko Duznovic, and Ivica Gavran." Now, can we agree that from this report it follows that Ivica Rajic decided to place these three persons in solitary confinement, and the reason he quotes is their attempt to obstruct planned activities? Does that follow from this report?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is page 3 you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Page 3, penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, Anto Pejcinovic, Zvonko Duznovic, and Ivica Gavran were indeed placed in solitary confinement in the afternoon on the 23rd of October, 1993, or maybe you don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which day, but I know one day, this -- it was 24 or 25, I could observe at the -- the police commander if the name was Ivica Gavran, I don't really remember, but it could be Gavran was sent away with a corps. He don't want or he couldn't talk to me because I have a problem this day. No commander want to talk to me. And I know him because I meet him a lot of times before. So I understand that he was sent away after -- maybe he was arrest, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Let's look together at what was actually happening with these people, including changes in the command of the Bobovac Brigade that you observed and that you reported. Let's look at document P 06039 in my set of documents.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: It's an interim report from Vitez area, dated 23rd October 1993, issued at 1900 hours. It's a very interesting document, but we'll focus only on the bottom part, the conclusion, the very end of this text. Request number 6. So the end of the document, "Conclusion," and request number 6. We see that it was signed by Tihomir Blaskic, commander of the military district of Central Bosnia. He says: "Commander of Operative Group 2, Mr. Ivica Rajic, is temporarily placed in isolation" -- sorry, "temporarily placed president of the Vares Croatian Defence Council, Mr. Anto Pejcinovic, in isolation for obstructing offensive actions against the Muslim armed forces, so I ask for your support. "I relieved certain members of the Brigade 'Bobovac' Command from their duty, particularly those that had been expecting the UN forces to defend them." Does it follow from this document, Witness, that Ivica Rajic decided to place Colonel Anto Pejcinovic in isolation?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can read that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Does it equally follow that changes in the command of Bobovac Brigade happened as a result of the decision of Tihomir Blaskic, commander of the military district of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Okay. Let us look now at 4D 00533. On the same day but a bit later, so on the 23rd October 1993, at 2245, Ivica Rajic informs Tihomir Blaskic as follows: "I don't think it would be a good idea now to change the brigade commander, but please give it some thought and give us your proposal as to who could perform this duty if Mr. Emil Harah is not in a position to be brigade commander." Mr. Birger, does it follow from this document that Ivica Rajic and his first direct superior communicated about who should lead Bobovac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't find the document but I know we change command on 23rd October.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: We'll see that in one of the following documents. Look at 4D 00532. The next day, 24th October at 8.50, Ivica Rajic reports to his immediate superior, Tihomir Blaskic --

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't find the document.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: 4D 00532. In my set of documents.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I couldn't find it. No, not 533.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: It's not 533, it's 532.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It was written. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: It's another short document. Ivica Rajic informs his immediate superior, Tihomir Blaskic, on the next day, 24th October, at 8.50, that Kresimir Bozic was authorised to command and control the brigade, and also that the brigade commander, Mr. Emil Harah, was allowed to go on a seven-day leave. Mr. Birger, you told us that Kresimir Bozic was in fact the person who led the Bobovac Brigade at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Did you know that Emil Harah was on sick leave for a while?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know why -- the reason why they change command. It's only in my opinion they change command this day.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: All right. Let us now look at what happened with Mr. Zvonko Duznovic. Look at document 4D 00528. Five minutes later, relative to the document we looked at before, Mr. Ivica Rajic sends a new proposal to his immediate superior, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic, namely that the chief of SIS of Bobovac Brigade, Zvonko Duznovic, be relieved of his duties. In the introductory part we read the reason, due to his destructive influence on the activities of the brigade, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can read that, and I don't really exactly remember the name of the members of the Bobovac Brigade, but I could recognise the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would object to this procedure whereby basically there's no foundation for this witness to do anything other than to confirm what's written in a series of orders. If there are questions about what he can testify about that, that's one thing, but simply to read a series of HVO documents to him with no foundation as to whether he's ever seen such documents or knew what was going on behind the scenes is -- is not a proper way to go forward, in our respectful view. He can certainly testify about people being relieved of command or changing positions based on his knowledge, but what was happening within the HVO command structure in terms of these orders or proposals or documents, there's simply no foundation at all that this witness had any knowledge about anything like that that was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you should have asked the witness whether he knew Zvonko Duznovic. He could answer yes or no. If he answered yes, then you could ask him whether to his knowledge Zvonko Duznovic was relieved of his functions. If yes or no, well, depending on that, you show the documents. Otherwise, he's going to read a document he doesn't know. Everybody knows this man doesn't know the document, and we're wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document showed to the witness by the Prosecutor, P 06117, mentions an alleged document by my client who reportedly authorised Ivica Rajic to relieve of duties Pejcinovic, Duznovic, and Gavran. My cross-examination had to do precisely with that part of the document. I believe that I have a full and legitimate right to try and show that such a document does not exist and the reasons why this is simply not possible. Secondly, as far as the documents I have so far shown to the witness, we did not stop to discuss these documents. I said that Kresimir Bozic, one the persons who was talked to, was indeed appointed a commander, and that Emil Harah was relieved of his duties, as the witness talked about this in his testimony. This is the first document I'm showing about Duznovic, and on the basis of the witness's statement I know that they communicated, inter alia, with Mr. Duznovic and that he knew his name. Now, I wanted to see if the witness could confirm whether Mr. Duznovic was indeed isolated, and I cannot know if the witness knows about this document or not unless I put the document to him first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, the witness can be asked about Duznovic and whether he knows whether or not Duznovic was relieved. Our objection goes more to the issue of whether the witness was aware of internal HVO documents discussing the -- discussing the issue of Mr. Duznovic and whether he had any knowledge as to who ordered what or who was proposing what or how these internal changes in terms of the leadership of that brigade came about, and that's an internal HVO matter and there's no foundation at all for this witness to be asked about proposals or orders or internal structural issues concerning the HVO and the Bobovac Brigade, and that's the basis of our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ms. Alaburic, what has been said now by Mr. Mundis seems to be justified. The witness is not aware of the HVO documents, and the very first answer he provided to Mr. Mundis during examination-in-chief showed that he even ignored the existence of the HVO. So based on that, the documents you've submitted to him have already been shown to another witness. We know these documents. We do. Do you think that this witness is going to make your case easier? If so, put him a question that is going to be useful to us. Otherwise, it's a waste of time. I don't mind being explained by a party what they are planning to do, but I need to understand. And here I fail to understand what you expect from the witness. You could ask him something that is going to enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since the Prosecution in this very courtroom on many occasions when addressing women who had nothing to do with the war operations whatsoever, who were housewives and who didn't know what their husbands were doing in the course of the day, showed them a series of HVO documents. We objected to that, and certain Judges -- or, rather, Judge Trechsel said that the witness can comment on a document if the witness is aware of the document's substance, regardless of the fact that the witness is unaware of who authored the document, when, and to whom it was sent. Now, the contents of the document were referred to as one of the bases for allowing the witness to be asked for comments. Now, I will not ask for the documents to be tendered. I simply cannot know all these matters beforehand, before I put -- I show the documents to the witness and put a question to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think the distinction here needs to be very clearly drawn. If a witness testifies about an event occurring on a certain date or a certain place at a certain time and there are documents that confirm what the witness knows from his or her own observations, then it's proper to show that witness those documents to confirm what the witness already knows based upon what they've observed. In this situation the documents relate to internal HVO matters concerning proposals, who proposed replacing whom, what decision was taken internally, and what was the source of that decision. That's a very different matter unless the witness can testify that he was present or saw these internal documents or saw these proposals or was present at meetings where these proposals were discussed. The witness very well might be able to testify about the ultimate issue in the sense of this commander was relieved or that person wasn't present any longer, but the process, the internal process by which that decision was taken is not a proper subject for him to be shown documents about unless he has an independent basis or observation or personal knowledge about how that decision-making process unfolded, and that is a distinction which is an important one, and it needs to be taken into consideration when witnesses are shown documents. If a crime base witness says, "My village was attacked by the HVO on this morning of this date," and we have an order or a combat report indicating that very fact, that confirms what the witness already knew. To show this witness or read to this witness documents about which person was proposing whom to be replaced is not a proper way, in our respectful submission, for documents to be dealt with and tends to result in huge amounts of time that are -- that could be used for more productive purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic, I'm listening. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to refer to something the Prosecutor just mentioned in his submission, and that's whether the witness knew someone or not. First of all, the witness, without having been asked said in his statement that Bozic replaced Harah, and there is nothing unclear there. The man noticed that Harah was removed and that Bozic took his place. Is that right, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, the ordinary brigade commander was -- was push away the 23rd of October and Kresimir -- Kresimir Bozic, or what the name, the former operational officer was the brigade commander. They changed this day. Why they changed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Petkovic very well. You know that they changed positions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Petkovic Witness, you conducted reconnaissance to deploy your forces and to get to know the commander of the Bobovac Brigade; is that right? This is something you said in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I meet him a lot of times before these days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but we are now -- Mr. Petkovic, I'm sorry. We are now speaking of someone else, someone called Duznovic. Did you know -- sorry, did you know Mr. Duznovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Kresimir Bozic. I couldn't remember names today. I have to look in my paper if want to, so I know only some -- which positions we had so on. I couldn't remember all names. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But did you know the chief of security of the Bobovac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was one person we was very lot talking together, and he was also -- when we was outside in the terrain, and maybe it was him I was talking to the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And were you aware of that person suddenly disappearing, sort of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't see him later this -- after this day. 24, 25, I don't meet them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think that's the basis on which Ms. Alaburic can present you with this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thought that what you just said is something everyone in the courtroom was aware of because the witness talked about it, and it was contained in the documents. I did not think it necessary to ask the witness whether he knew Zvonko Duznovic since the witness had already talked about it. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to thank Judge Trechsel because this is precisely what I would like to ask the witness. And I would like to say that the statement that the witness said, that once he sat in the Bobovac Brigade HQ for five hours waiting for someone with this person. Is that right, Witness? And that this person who was there with you spoke some English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I have said so in the statement, that's correct. If the statement says so, yes. I know I was there a lot of hours this day, and I have no contact with commanders. I only talk with one member of the Bobovac Brigade. That's correct. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm aware of that. I listened carefully to what you had to say, and I am surprised to hear that some others didn't know. Your Honours, therefore this witness knew the person -- persons, was in touch with them, and then noticed that suddenly they did not hold these positions any longer. And now he's being shown documents which show that some persons that he used to be in touch with were not there any longer. I don't see that there is any problem with what my counsel is trying to show here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just add, and I would like to thank my colleague Nozica, one section of his statement which says, "security officer, Duznovic, whose English was very poor, told me that Emil Harah was ill." So this is the link.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Witness, now we have established you knew who Zvonko Duznovic was and that for a while he was absent. Let's look at 4D 0028 that we had here a moment ago -- 4D 00528. Did you have any knowledge to the effect that Rajic took steps to relieve of duty Duznovic? 4D 00528.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can read that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about such an initiative having been launched?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but -- but I know --

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when I talked to him this day before the men came from Kiseljak. What he said, "It was a bad day for them. It was a bad day for the Bobovac Brigade."

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, were you aware of the fact that later on some proceedings were initiated against Duznovic investigating all criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean in this question, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. If you had any knowledge about it, then I would show you some documents indicating what were the steps that Blaskic took in this regard, but let's move on. Do you know who Ivica Gavran was in Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. If I may remember right, he was, so to say, the police commander. I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: According to your information, on the 23rd of October, was he also placed in isolation?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. In my opinion, he was -- if he was the man who was the police commander -- I could mix names here. So he was for -- away with the corps and I think it was the 24th of October, from the headquarter, Bobovac Brigade. I tried to talk to him but they don't allow me to do it. They put him in the car and the car was driving on to Tuzla direction, not to Vares.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: We will not be analysing that. Let us look at another document to see whether you knew what became of the initiative to relieve him of duty. Let's look at document P 09813. That's in my set of documents. We've already seen this document in this courtroom. At this point I should be interested only in the last sentence. First of all, Ivica Rajic is addressing the chief of the police administration in Travnik, Mr. Mladen Tolo, and the last sentence: "For the reasons well known, initiate proceedings for relieving Ivica Gavran of duty." Did you know anything about this initiative to relieve Ivica Gavran from his position in Vares, Witness?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know Anto Pejcinovic? He was the president of the Vares HVO.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Did you know that he was placed in isolation in the afternoon hours of the 23rd of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I couldn't meet him. He was also one of them I want to talk to but I don't could have any contact with him. I meet him some days later in Dastansko. In November.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see him in the course of October, because he was released on the 25th. Did you perhaps see him in Vares at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Birger, I thank you for your answers. Let us move to a different topic now, which in a way picks up from that map shown to you by Mr. Praljak. Let us go through several documents and see if and for how long the BH army was planning offensive activities in Vares. I will also show you documents authored before your arrival in Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to sustain whether the later developments --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could Madam Alaburic repeat the last part of her question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Let us start with document 4D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask you, Madam Alaburic, to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't come to the question yet. I was explaining the witness what we're about to do.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I'm intending to show you documents drafted before your arrival in Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to establish whether the events you're familiar with were consistent with what was observed or planned several months earlier. If you're unfamiliar with these documents, we will be finished with them quite soon. Please look at document 4D 00526. This is a document by the military police intelligence service of the command of the military district of Central Bosnia, dated the 12th of August, 1993. Briefly, the document is interesting in several of its particulars. The third item of the document says: "The road to Kopjari is quite unsafe."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps to save time, you have announced, Ms. Alaburic, that you would first ask the witness if he knows the document or not and then ask him about it. Perhaps you could follow that plan you have established.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I didn't say that. I'm not intending to ask the witness whether he knew the document but, rather, whether the later developments taking part -- happening at the time when he was in the area were consistent with the documents that were written earlier. The documents are HVO reports and plans by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm referring to what you say on, I think it is page 68, the second and third line. "If you're unfamiliar with these documents, we'll be finished with them quite soon." So wouldn't it be consequent if you ask him whether he is familiar so then we know whether you are finished soon with them?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I intend to ask the witness about some of the contents of the documents, then I have to refer to the contents first. I'm very interested in hearing about the part concerning Stupni Do on the 23rd of October. That part will be very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. I was trying to be helpful and to help you save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, we would again ask that a proper foundation be laid, and also perhaps the relevance of any BH army plans concerning what -- what transpired during the month of October and into early November 1993. It's a bit unclear what the basis of asking this witness about documents that are dated several months before he even arrived in theatre, not to mention the relevance of any potential BH army plans in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you can introduce the document by asking a question. The first line actually allows you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. This has to do with the activities of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I will tell you why it is that I'm putting these questions. One of the relevant facts in this case is the fact that the military units from -- came from Kiseljak to Vares. Therefore, Vares needed the assistance from other HVO units. I wish to show why this was happening, and I wish to show the extent of the offensive activities of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I also wish to show that the Bobovac Brigade alone could in no way prevent Vares from falling. I also wish to demonstrate that the BH army had systematically been planning offensive activities. And my final question will show that, unfortunately, for the better part of these activities they were successful.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, when you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina, specifically in the Vares area, did you have any knowledge about the strength of the BH army forces, for instance, in Stupni Do and the inhabited areas around Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about Stupni Do. If I have any information about Stupni Do, that should be a Muslim village inside Bobovac Brigade area. I immediately sent down soldiers from my company where it was one of the reason I sent soldier up in the Kopjari area to observe down in the village of Mijakovici and Dragovici. I don't have no information about Stupni Do. But first day I heard about Stupni Do was in Bobovac Brigade the morning of 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Witness, now you mentioned the villages of Mijakovici and Dragovici. Please look at the third paragraph of this document 4 -- P 02526. It says by beginning control over Kopjari the Muslim villages of Mijakovici and Dragovici would have a road connection to Kakanj through the Bukovica canyon?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. I will not be asking you about the remainder of the document. Let's look at document 4D 00523. 4D 00523. This document was issued by Stjepan Siber, deputy commander of the BH army, on the 21st of August, 1993, and it is addressed to the command of the 3rd Corps. The first sentence reads: "Taking into consideration all the facts laid out in the analysis and --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hate to interrupt but again our objection goes to the issue of relevance. "What is the relevance of BH army plans with respect to these villages in the municipality of Vares as they relate to the indictment in this case?" We believe that this -- there's been evidence that these attacks took place. There's been evidence that puts this into the proper context, but we believe day point that that is irrelevant to the charges that have been -- that have been laid against these accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In fact, Ms. Alaburic, the objection made by the Prosecutor is sound, in fact. We saw the map presented by General Praljak not long ago where we could see that Vares was circled and we saw that this was the result of the offensive of the ABiH army. I understand, but with regard to the relevancy to the indictment and the facts that are -- that exist in the indictment, how can this be useful to your case? I fail to see the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, some of the BH army documents, including some news reports from the BH media, it might be concluded that there were positions that the fall of Vares came as a result of the HVO attack on Stupni Do. What I wish to demonstrate with this document is that the offensive against Vares had been planned for several months, that the events taking place in and around Vares that this witness referred to were part of a plan that had been systematically implemented over several months. I believe that this is a context which is necessary in order to get the whole picture of the events in Vares, with the exception of the events at Stupni Do, which were not then immediate consequence of the military action. This is one topic that I will not be discussing with the witness at all. Therefore, with this document I wish to prove that the Supreme Command of the armed forces in the month of August 1993, approved the plan of the 3rd Corps for offensive activities in the general area of -- in the broader area of Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. President, that's certainly an explanation for why my learned colleague proposes to proceed in this fashion, but it doesn't, with all due respect, give to the issue of relevance and how this line of questioning has anything to do with the charges in the indictment other than to say it involved ABiH plans for offensive operations in Vares municipality. In what way does that relate to the charges or provide a defence for any of these accused with respect to the events as they eventually unfolded? It is not relevant to the charges in this indictment. It might be quite interesting from a political or military or historical perspective, but it's not relevant to this indictment, and for that reason we object to this line of questioning being allowed to continue. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] This indictment explicitly speaks of the joint criminal enterprise that these six persons, to the with some non-existent and dead people planned to attack the BH army, the unprotected Muslim civilian population, et cetera. The document we are producing or showing and wish to demonstrate that it is exactly the opposite. Despite all the support from Croatia in arms and otherwise, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Konjic to over places conducted systematic attacks -- attacks against the HVO, bringing in crowds of people who were out of control, who could have perpetrated and did perpetrate crimes. It is precisely the basis of this indictment who attacked whom, how, who supported whom, who provided weapons to whom, et cetera. Or shall we return to the individual basis? In Stupni Do, who exactly committed crimes and when, but then, in that case, it would have nothing to do with this group of people and this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's -- it's unclear -- it's unclear from what Mr. Praljak has just indicated, but to the extent any of the Defence teams are moving towards some kind of tu quoque defence, that is an improper, impermissible defence for the type of charges that are in this indictment, and if that is what is emerging, then the Prosecution with all due respect would like to be heard on that at greater length at some point in the near future. The fact of the matter is, the kind of charges in the indictment regarding Vares municipality have little or nothing to do with ABiH plans with respect to attacks on villages in that municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: As I view this, there is in the air an allegation that the HVO engaged in manoeuvres to have the ABiH, as it were, assist them in -- in contrary cleansing, driving Croats out of the Vares area in order to create more Croatic -- Croat regions elsewhere. I think that is part of the indictment in a larger sense, and therefore I quite agree with Mr. Praljak's thing, and I think in that respect the questioning can continue. It's another question whether the witness can say much about that that you will want to see, but otherwise, I would say proceed. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you very much. If somebody prepares an offensive for months after expelling 15.000 Kakanj locals --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I have stopped you when you made negative comments on what I said, and I also stop you when you make positive comments. I think you should not comment. We should continue. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] One more thing, please. There's something that is clear as day in law. One crime cannot justify another, and that is legally obvious. But since the beginning of times we know that, sociologically speaking, one crime gives rise to another. Law does not justify that, but law has never prevented one crime for giving rise to another. Those are two separate things. Legal formulations are one thing, and another thing is the reality that crime triggers crime. Those are two separate things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Trechsel, very much for this intercession, and maybe after this debate we should take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 25 past. We'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. We have 55 minutes left. The Trial Chamber demands that the testimony of this witness is completed today. Ms. Alaburic, you have some time left. You've reviewed a lot of documents. Some of them you still want to reconsider or examine with the witness. I understand that Mr. Mundis has some re-examination, but my fellow Judge also has a question to put to the witness that is in the logical sequence of the questions you've put yourself. So I think it's better if he puts the question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I can -- I can -- if you think it is up to -- Mr. Birger, I wanted to ask after the 23rd of October, during the time of the 23rd to the 25th of October and the 3rd to 5th of November, you had conversations with interlocutors from the HVO in which the subject of Stupni Do and the reasons for it would come up and whether you have heard opinions on -- and appreciations on what had happened there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first the information I had was the 23rd of October, and they informed me that they had attacked Mir, I mean the 6th Corps, and also they have attacked the village of Stupni Do, belonged to the logistics line and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. I may have not have quite clear in my question. I am wondering about appreciations, justifications, bad feelings, positive feelings, explanations rather than the sheer information which we have already covered, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was different between us. We was very friendly before the 23rd, and this day they don't want to talk to us, and the next -- in the evening they also threaten us, said, "If you don't take the APCs inside and so on we are going to destroy it." So it changed from very friendly contact to be not so friendly, so to say, and what was going on with days in the last of October until they leave Vares area to village of Dastansko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And were you told anything about -- about Stupni Do, whether it was justified or whether it was a big mistake or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. We -- I tried don't talk so much about it because we had another problem to solve in the city, but we do it, and when my interpreter tell me after when I talk about that, a lot -- some of the officers or soldiers in Bobovac Brigade headquarters was sitting behind me and laughing. And the next time I was there I was waiting for -- for the Kresimir Bozic, this soldier was saying something in Serbo-Croat, and my interpreter translated and said, "Are you here now again to talk about Stupni Do," and they start laughing. I remember that very well because we were so angry - it was me and our interpreter - so we was very, very -- it was very, very close to be fighting to this young man, because we were so angry about they was laughing about what was happening in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to discuss with you Stupni Do and the resulting investigations, but let us first finish the text that we started. We worked through 4D 00523, and then let's finish with it. It will take just five minutes. 4D 00523. So that's a document issued by deputy commander of the BH army, Stjepan Siber, to the command of the 3rd Corps giving his opinion about the plan of offensive operations in the broader area of Vares. In point 1, it says: We agree with your suggestions on launching offensive activities towards Lijesnica feature as well as along the direction of Jezero. Tell me, Mr. Birger, when you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you witness the capture of Lijesnica feature by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't really remember the name of Lijesnica. I remember Jezero hill because I was up there in the middle of October, and the Borovica I also know about, but nothing about Lijesnica or -- excuse me for the name. I don't remember that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think there is probably a misprint probably in the transcript, because the text that you read has the words, "offensive activities with limited objective," and I'm sure you also read this, and that's written in the transcript so perhaps that could be corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. The counsel didn't really quote. She just gave a brief summary of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I referred only to point 1 in the introductory part -- I didn't read the introductory part at all. In the introductory part we read about offensive operations in the broader area of Vares.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Another thing I'm interested in is in point 3. There is a reference to Ilijas -- sorry, Plijes feature. Did you witness the capture of this feature by the army?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this village in the middle of -- at the beginning of what I was to recognising the area and this day, I don't remember exactly which day it was, there were no soldiers in Miljakovic and Dragovici. I was down in this village with 20 of October. I put soldiers up in Kopjari and, when I give orders, I get down with one APC to these two village, and it was clear different this day, 20 of October. It was a lot of soldiers there and I was more or less not so very welcome there. And what I could understand, they use some path down to Kakanj area.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You said you were not welcome. You mean you did not feel that you were really welcome as far as the BH army was concerned?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think they don't want me to be there. In my opinion, I -- I'm a professional officer. I understand very well that they were doing. They was preparing an attack of Kopjari.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look at 4D 00524, dated 18 October 1993. The commander of the 2nd Corps, Hazim Sadic. I will summarise the document which is relatively brief. He says that units of the 3rd Corps, on the 17th of October, launched an attack against the positions of Bobovac Brigade in the areas of Lijesnica, Kopjari, and Plijes. I'm skipping a bit now. But before that I want to ask you can you confirm that the BH army did indeed mount an attack on HVO positions on the said features on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly which day, but it was some days before the 21st of October. It was firing some attacks both in -- from Planinica around Kopjari up to Borovica. It was small fighting there and I remember it was some policemen or soldiers from Bobovac Brigade. One or two was killed. Two or three was wounded, and they sent them to the field hospital in 2nd Corps area.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you know the total strength of the 2nd and the 3rd Corps of the BH army respectively? Do you know that the total strength of these two could have been 40.000?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea about how many. Nothing about that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Generally speaking, in military terminology, what does a corps imply in terms of number?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's about so many. I don't think it is so many, because the strength of a brigade was not normally brigade strength in -- it was more or less a battalion strength, each brigade. It's my opinion about it. But if it was so many soldiers I don't know. I never saw so many soldiers down in different parts in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Birger, can we now look at some HVO documents and see what the assessments of Vares HVO were, whether they thought they had enough strength to counter the offensive of the BH army. Can we first look at 4D 00522. 522. You have found it?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: We're looking for 522.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: That's also 18 October 1993. If we recall the previous document of the BH army, it was of the same date. Brigade commander of the Bobovac Brigade reports to HVO in Tuzla about an attack against the HVO in Vares area. In item 2 it says, "Lines in the areas of Lijesnica, Kopjari, Plijes, and Jezero were vigorously attacked." Can we confirm that those are the same localities as mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect from -- that's incorrect from what -- in my opinion what's happening in the area at which time.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Right. Can you repeat your answer, because the interpreter didn't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean is in these days in October, we know what they was fighting -- small fighting. It was impact in the village of Borovica, that's correct, in -- actually, mortars. It was also correct that it was fighting in the village of Slavin and also small arm firing in Kopjari. And one day when I was there they also have used -- they, I mean the 3rd Corps, have also used some type of anti-tank 40 or 20-millimetre cannon to firing up on the village. So I think that can be correct what's written here.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: In point 5, the commander of the Bobovac Brigade expresses his misgivings that this offensive could be joined by members of the 2nd Corps as well. Did you have any inkling that the 2nd Corps could join in this attack? Just briefly, did you have any such information or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in these days, in the 23rd of October, because, as I said before, the forces in -- in 2nd Corps in Olovo and so on, they was friendly to Bobovac Brigade, and they also sent -- Bobovac Brigade also sent wounded soldiers into the field hospital west of Kakanj -- Kladanj. So for me it was no fighting again, the 2nd Corps and the Bobovac Brigade, not now.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look at 4D 00527. Again commander of the Bobovac Brigade, Emil Harah. This time on the 22nd October addresses Ivica Rajic in Kiseljak, and in item it 2 he says the situation is critical because it is impossible to get reinforcements and to communicate up to Kopjari, and it is impossible to have the communication necessary for supply and medical support. "We have injured men," et cetera, et cetera, "and we need assistance in manpower and ammunition." Do you know how many troops Bobovac Brigade had? Well, let me help you. Are you aware that their strength was around 1.500 men?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many men they was, but in my military terms it was very, very little force, little unit up in Kopjari. It was only handful so to say. It was not, in my opinion, enough to defend the area. And I can -- I can also agree what is written here in the point of 1 that the attack came from the village of Dragovici.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that. Tell us, Mr. Birger, since you communicated almost daily with the commander of Bobovac Brigade, did anyone tell you during those days that they needed assistance in troops and that they had asked Ivica Rajic for -- for such assistance in manpower and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: All right. Let us now look at 4D 00530. It's an interim report from the chief of the Military Intelligence Service of Bobovac Brigade from these services in Vitez and Kiseljak, dated 23rd October, 1993. It says: "This morning an extremely fierce attack began against Kopjari and Borovica villages." It says, furthermore, that the defence of Vares is in a crisis. Experienced men are needed to help out. Can you confirm, Mr. Birger, that indeed on the 21st of October Kopjari and Borovica villages were attacked, and they eventually came under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, if I remember right, maybe it was 5.30, 6.00. Early in the morning the attack was started to Kopjari, and they take only some hours for the BH army to take control of Kopjari. I was up in the area just before lunch, what's mean 11.00, between 11.00, 12.00, and it was heavy fighting in the wood in that area north of Kopjari. So in that moment, the village was falling, Kopjari was falling. I also remember there was some impact of mortars in the village of Borovica, and also what the HVO tried to shelling the village of Dragovici with mortar, but it was, so to say, impact in -- before the village, north of the village. It was also -- I can say we find two or three HVO soldiers. One of them, I talked to him before I leave, the evening before, the day before. They came with woman and tell me it had been some massacre in the village, and we said, "Okay. Show me the massacre." And I send one of my military policemen and one of my officers to the place, and they come back and report to me they was falling in action. They was hit here falling in his trench and so on. And one of the soldier was wounded, but he have been dead some hour after he was -- they have tried to help him with first aid like this, but he was also dead. Two or three. I think it was three dead HVO soldiers in the village of Kopjari.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Can we agree, Mr. Birger, that after the fall of Kopjari village the defence of Vares was really in a critical situation?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was, in my military opinion. If I had some mechanised units they could take the village, but on this, down because the road was more or less opened onto Vares.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Right. Let us now look at 4D 00531. Item 4, the last sentence. It's a document generated by Kresimir Bozic, who was then on the command of Bobovac Brigade on the 21st of October, and the last sentence - this is addressed to Ivica Rajic - reads: "It is my personal belief without your presence in our zone of responsibility further developments will not provide for efficient defence of Vares." Can we agree that commanders of Bobovac Brigade then believed there was no way they can defend Vares without outside help?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can understand that. That why they try to have military help.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. On the 23rd of October, the HVO attacks Stupni Do. We saw parts of other documents that describe how Stupni Do was defended. Now please look at 4D 00530. 520, sorry. It's a document issued by Abdulah Ahmic, commander. It's from the 6th Corps. Command of Operative Group east. We can read it. It's relatively short. "In view of the deteriorating situation in the area of responsibility of the Vares Municipal Defence Staff, escalating combat operations, especially in Stupni Do village area, which has been under fierce combined artillery and infantry attacks by the Ustashas since early morning and is entirely surrounded, and in the order to help break the blockade of the village of Stupni Do, I hereby order. "Keep Breza ready to be engaged in combat along the axis of attack, pursuant to Breza commander's decision," et cetera. This document is important to us in trying to answer the question: Did the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina plan to assist its own unit that was defending Stupni Do? Do you have any knowledge about such plans by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never seen this document before. It is first time. But I know that there was fighting in the area of this morning from the south. That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, several days after the 23rd. 4D 00525. 525. Yes, it's the correct number. It's an order by the commander of the BH army, Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: To the commander of the 3rd Corps, it says: "The command of the 2nd Corps addressed a request that the 3rd Corps be engaged in executing our orders of the 26th October 1993." I'm skipping all this large bit. Paragraph 1: "Units of the 3rd Corps designated for offensive activities against Ustasha forces of Vares are to be immediately engaged along given routes and linked up with 2nd Corps forces in the area of Kozja Glavica feature." You confirmed, Witness, looking at this map and otherwise that Vares fell in the course of the offensive action mounted by the 2nd and the 3rd Corps jointly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Can we just confirm on the basis of this document that this link-up of the 2 Corps happened as a result of the order of the Supreme Commander of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to be so, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Look at 4D 00518. It's a document made by commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, Amir Kubura. Right now I would appreciate it if you could just comment on point 4. "Upon return to base, fighting men should go home, and the next few days should be used for dividing the booty." Could you tell us what could be that booty to be distributed among the men of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what, they tried looting a lot of when they came into -- into Vares. We tried to stop them. We stopped them at the Catholic church. We stopped them at the two stores. I think it was from the UNHCR store and some other help organisations. But what type or what it was they distribute, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I ask, Ms. Alaburic, apart from tu quoque, what is the relevance of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, it was not my intention by any means to justify any possible similar actions by the HVO. I thought instead it was a relevant question because it tells us about the fear on the part of the Croatian population before the on-coming Muslim army and that speaks to the charge in the indictment that Croats fabricated and made up bad conducts on the part of the BH army to stimulate people to leave towards other areas. Otherwise, they were stoking the fears of their own Croat population. But I just -- I'm just saying this so that the witness can know what to expect, where I'm getting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I seem to have up stood that they had practically all left before the 7th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but it's -- the question is why they left. Did they leave because the HVO or the civilian authorities of the HVO spread rumours about misdeeds of the Muslim army that were not true in order to stimulate Croats to leave Central Bosnia, including Vares, or was it because of some events that justified the fears of Croat civilians of what might happen when Vares and if Vares is indeed captured by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Witness, at this moment I'm holding a document that unfortunately I cannot show you, but I can read a part of it to you. It's from Commander Hazim Sadic. Let me remind you, it's the commander of the 2nd Corps. 2nd December, 1993. It says: "From members of NordBat the commander of the 2nd Corps learned that members of the civilian police from Lasta and other units are rounded up and mistreating Croat civilians who remained in Vares. They even take civilians over from NordBat."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you didn't include this document. You show it at the last minute. So this is putting us into a difficult situation, because we don't know anything about this document. Furthermore, it's not translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't prepare this document for the testimony of this witness, but I used it now simply because the issue was raised as to whether I want to ask this witness about war booty in order to try and level out the conduct on both of the sides, but this is not my intention. I intend to show that the Croatian population from Vares and other areas left out of fear of possible actions from the BH army, and that's why I, in this context, wanted to show this fact. We wanted to show about the conduct of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood. Colonel, I'm going to ask you something because you were there in the area of Vares, end October, beginning of November, and you witnessed the departure of the population, the Croatian population, as they left Vares. Can you tell us why the Croatian population of Vares left? It is a very simple question. Can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I don't remember exactly which day, but it was the day before HVO leaved Vares by travelling -- by use vehicles with low -- with what -- I couldn't find the word in English, but they use like this. They use loudspeaker to speak out to the people, "You must leave, you must leave, the Muslims are coming," and so on. And what I remember, and it was a lot of people. There was thousand of them down in between Vares and the village of Dastansko, and the last day they hold Vares, the HVO, it was also hundreds of civilians outside the Bobovac headquarter. So in my opinion they be more or less ordered to leave by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said on line 14, "The Muslims are coming." In saying so, did they mean to tell the population there was some danger, that they had to go? How do you interpret the words used through the megaphones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was information I have from my soldier down in -- in Vares, and how we have that information directly how it was translated, I don't know. I don't hear it myself. I was this day out in the terrain, but it was -- remember, it was also written down in our reports, so to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, in your statements you that the HVO, by using a vehicle and loudspeaker, announced that a general mobilisation was carried out in order to mount a defence of Vares; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had said so in my statement, it's right, yes. I remember also it was some message out that they should mobilise all men. And they have tried to do it with refugees, some weeks before.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, you also testified before this Tribunal in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Mundis, how many minutes do you need for your redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seven minutes. So you have another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Birger, you testified in the proceedings against Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Kubura before this Tribunal; is that right? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's some years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Defence counsel during their cross-examination tried to make you say that the HVO forced Croats out of Vares? Do you recall that on the location they explained to you how every day at the Bobovac Brigade HQ you met with HVO representatives and that this was the reason why you were on good terms with them?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't --

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You don't recall that, do you?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, it was -- I can't remember everything this day. I must go back to -- to what I do -- say in the statement. It's -- it's -- what I have said there is what I remember best.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have the transcript with your testimony here, but I'm speaking from memory, and you said in that testimony that one could not say that the HVO forced Croats to leave the Vares area. Hence my question to you: Did you or any of your colleagues see, observe the HVO forcing any Croats to leave Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They only inform them with loudspeakers. I couldn't say that they forced them out, but I understand they was afraid so therefore they escape. But also to add that, not all people leave Vares. There was some Croat people even very often after that attack.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. My time is up. I would have many questions for you but under the time constraints I have to thank you, Mr. Birger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Birger, I have a few questions for you and to the best of your recollection let's try to be clear on this, to the best of your recollection on what day did the civilian population, for the most part, leave the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that exactly, but it was before one or two days, maybe three days before the southern Muslim brigade came into the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And on what day, to the best of your recollection, did the Bobovac Brigade withdraw from the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, if I remember right, the morning of the 3rd of November. It was the day before -- it was one day. I mean, they leave that morning. This morning they leave the Bobovac Brigade. It was burning and there was only one or two policemen down in the square of Vares and then everything was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then to the best of your recollection, sir, on what day did the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina enter the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: HAKAN BIRGER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, if I remember right, the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
